### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.operators

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Using both `mini.ai` (not required, but allows better control/knowledge of how the textobjects for the operators are selected) and `mini.operators` default configuration, given the buffer

```lua
foo(
  a,
  b,
  c
)
```

, and with the cursor above `a`, doing `yi)` and then `gri)` results in the buffer

```lua
foo
  a,
  b,
  c

)
```

while I would expect it to result in the same buffer. Similar results can be seen with the multiply operator. `gmi)` results in

```lua
foo(
  a,
  b,
  c(
  a,
  b,
  c
)
```

note the `(` after `c` that should not be part of the textobject.

This happens because in

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9b935c218ddba02e5dc75c94f90143bce1f7c646/lua/mini/operators.lua#L1167-L1171

`keys` ends up being something similar to `` `["_dv`] ``. Then, when Neovim moves the cursor to the `[` mark, since it isn't on visual mode and `virtualedit` default value is empty, instead of putting the cursor on the newline after `(`, the cursor is placed on the parenthesis itself.

This issue can be (partially) solved by temporarily changing `virtualedit` to `onemore` inside of 

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9b935c218ddba02e5dc75c94f90143bce1f7c646/lua/mini/operators.lua#L1149

(like it is already done on `mini.ai` for selecting a textobject). After that change, the first example no longer deletes the `(`, but it still duplicates the newline after `c`. So the end result is

```lua
foo(
  a,
  b,
  c

)
```

I've been look at it for a while, but I'm not sure as to why. Yanking (`yi)`) includes the trailing newline after `c` and `mini.ai` tries to move the cursor to `{4, 4}` when selecting the textobject. But, replacing `gri)`does not include the trailing newline after `c` when deleting the text. `vim.api.nvim_buf_get_mark(0, ']')` returns `{4, 2}` and `` `] `` moves the cursor up to `c`. So, my guess is that this second part of the issue may have something to do with Neovim internals (?

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
    local clone_cmd = { "git", "clone", "--depth=1", "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim", mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim")
    require("mini.deps").setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub

    require("mini.ai").setup()
    require("mini.operators").setup()
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Insert the following text in the buffer

```
foo(
  a,
  b,
  c
)
```

5. Put the cursor above `a`, `yi)` and `gri)`

The resulting buffer will be

```
foo
  a,
  b,
  c

)

```

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

Yeah, these kind of edge cases are hard to fix; especially in 'mini.operators' since it has to deal with all kinds of Vim motions/selections edge cases. To the point when I am tempted to describe this as a known limitation. But would indeed first require an investigation and an honest attempt to fix this in a reasonably concise way.

> This issue can be (partially) solved by temporarily changing `virtualedit` to `onemore` inside of

Yeah, that would be my first idea to try if it is not already.

> I've been look at it for a while, but I'm not sure as to why.

If you wouldn't find the issue in 'mini.operators' or Neovim (or probably Vim's) behavior, I'll take look (hopefully) tomorrow.

While staring at the problem with the trailing newline I realized that `replace` is also broken in visual mode when the textobject has newlines at start/end. Even after #2248 . Moving the temporary `virtualedit=onemore` even higher up the call stack (so it is active for both the deleting and pasting steps) seems to also solve the issue for leading newlines in visual char mode

It also seems like custom textobjects can't know if the last line of the textobject has a trailing newline.

I created the simply operator

```lua
---@param type 'line'|'char'|'block'
_G.my_yank = function(type)
  local mode = type == "line" and "V" or type == "char" and "v" or vim.keycode "<c-v>"
  local yanked = vim.fn.getregion(vim.fn.getpos "'[", vim.fn.getpos "']", { type = mode })
  -- __PRINT_VAR_START
  print([==[┆_G.my_yank┆ ╎yanked╎ ┊1┊:]==], vim.inspect(yanked)) -- __PRINT_VAR_END
end
vim.keymap.set({ "x", "n" }, "<F4>", function(a)
  vim.o.operatorfunc = "v:lua._G.my_yank"
  return "g@"
end, { expr = true })
```

and opened the buffer

```
foo(
  a,
  b,
  c
)
```

both `<f4>i)` and `vi)<f4>` print the last line as `  c`, no matter if the cursor in visual mode is above the `c` or one character to the right (so, above the newline).

However, builtin operators like `y` and `d` seem to make a distinction between both cases for visual mode (if the cursor if above the `c`, the newline is not deleted/yanked, if the cursor is one character to the right the newline is deleted/yanked). Doing `di)` and `yi)` correctly includes the trailling newline.

I also realized that after `vi)<f4>` the value of the mark `]` was `{4,2}`, but  the value of the mark `>` was `{4,3}`. However, changing the textobject to

```lua
---@param type 'line'|'char'|'block'
_G.my_yank = function(type)
  if vim.api.nvim_get_mode().mode == "v" then vim.cmd.normal(vim.keycode "<c-\\><c-n>") end

  local mode = type == "line" and "V" or type == "char" and "v" or vim.keycode "<c-v>"
  local yanked = vim.fn.getregion(vim.fn.getpos "'<", vim.fn.getpos "'r", { type = mode })
  -- __PRINT_VAR_START
  print([==[┆_G.my_yank┆ ╎yanked╎ ┊1┊:]==], vim.inspect(yanked)) -- __PRINT_VAR_END
end
vim.keymap.set({ "x", "n" }, "<F4>", function(a)
  vim.o.operatorfunc = "v:lua._G.my_yank"
  return "g@"
end, { expr = true })
```

and doing `vi)<f4>` still does not include the trailling newline.

Based on that information, I think that it should be possible to account for the trailing newline if using `nvim_` API functions and only for visual char mode. But, I think that it's not possible to do so for both visual mode and textobjects, specially when using normal mode commands directly.

I've opened https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/37664 on the Neovim repo. The limitation of custom operators not being able to distinguish between regions with and without a trailing newline (while builtin operators are able to) comes from the C implementation of both. So, it seems like we can't do anything about the trailing newline in the `mini.nvim` side of things.

I'll slightly modify #2248 to temporarily change `onemore` upper in the call stack (probably on each `MiniOperators.xxx` function) to account for the bug on `MiniOperators.Replace` that's present on `MiniOperators.replace` only in visual mode mentioned earlier. After that, It should be ready to be merged

This should now be fixed on latest `main` as best as it can reasonably do. More details in [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/2248#issuecomment-3842500619).

Thanks again for spotting this and researching about the solution.

title: [mini.operators] some operators have issues with newlines at start/end of textobject
